title: MM-MT103-ParentChildSessionRegistry

scope.summary:
GOAL: Durable parent-child session lineage: a PostgreSQL-backed registry of who spawned whom, with a max-depth limit, cycle prevention, and a cascade policy when a parent terminates. This is the canonical lineage source consumed by MT-102 (steer scope), MT-105 (notification routing), MT-107 (session tree GUI), and MT-108 (cascade proof).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: One new numbered migration pair (up + .down.sql) in src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/ creating table `swarm_session_lineage`; a new module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/session_lineage.rs (store + queries + depth/cycle guards + cascade executor); wiring in the MT-101 spawn handler (attach on spawn) and coordinator terminal-state observation (detach + cascade on parent termination). Tests.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Table `swarm_session_lineage` rows: `parent_session_id` (text, not null), `child_session_id` (text, not null, unique), `spawned_by_actor` (text: `model:<parent_session_id>` | `operator` | `scheduler`), `role_id` (text nullable), `created_at_utc` (timestamptz), `terminated_at_utc` (timestamptz nullable), plus `cascade_policy` (text: `orphan` | `cascade_cancel`) captured at attach time. Indexes on parent_session_id and child_session_id. Paired down migration.
2. Max depth: config `model_to_model.max_spawn_depth` default 2 (operator > orchestrator model > worker; a worker may not spawn by default). Attach computes the chain depth by walking parents; exceeding depth returns typed `DepthExceeded` and the MT-101 handler rejects the spawn BEFORE calling spawn_session.
3. Cycle prevention: attach rejects any row where child_session_id already appears in the caller's ancestor chain (typed `LineageCycle`). Because child ids are coordinator-minted fresh ids, a cycle indicates id reuse or spoofing and is also ledgered as an anomaly.
4. Cascade policy on parent termination: default `cascade_cancel` — when a parent session reaches a terminal state, all live children are cancelled through the coordinator's existing cancellation/teardown path (never direct process kill), depth-first, each cancellation ledgered. `orphan` mode (per-spawn opt-in, policy-gated by MT-106) leaves children running with `spawned_by_actor` attribution intact and marks the row orphaned.
5. FR events: stamp attach and detach using existing SwarmFrEventId events enriched with lineage payload fields (parent_session_id, depth, cascade_policy); NEW event kinds (e.g. a dedicated lineage-attach id) belong to MT-161's FR-kind seam — this MT only enriches payloads of existing SESSION-SPAWNED / SESSION-CANCELLED / SESSION-COMPLETED / SESSION-FAILED events and records registry rows.
6. Read API for consumers: `children_of(parent)`, `parent_of(child)`, `ancestor_chain(child)`, `live_tree(root)` — used by MT-102 lineage checks and the MT-107 tree GUI.

SECURITY FRAME (binding): lineage rows are attribution evidence — attach/detach happen server-side in the spawn/terminate paths only; no tool or model can write lineage rows directly. Depth limit and cycle guard bound recursive self-spawning (HBR-SWARM-001/002: a runaway orchestrator cannot build an unbounded tree even under the coordinator's global caps).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the latest migration number in src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/ and take the next free prefix; author up + down SQL.
2. Implement session_lineage.rs store with attach/detach/queries and depth/cycle guards; PostgreSQL only (no SQLite path on this write surface).
3. Wire attach into the MT-101 spawn handler (after policy pass, before spawn_session; roll back the row if spawn_session rejects).
4. Wire detach + cascade into the coordinator terminal-state event observation (subscribe to session terminal events; do not modify coordinator internals beyond the existing event/observer seam).
5. Implement cascade_cancel depth-first cancellation via coordinator cancellation API; ledger each cancelled child.
6. Tests per expected_tests.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/** (next free numeric prefix only; paired .down.sql)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs (observe via existing event seam only; no internal edits)
acceptance_criteria: Migration creates swarm_session_lineage with the specced columns/indexes and a working down migration; runs green against managed PostgreSQL.
Every MT-101 model-initiated spawn writes exactly one lineage row server-side; no tool surface can write lineage rows directly.
Spawn attempts beyond model_to_model.max_spawn_depth (default 2) are rejected with typed DepthExceeded BEFORE spawn_session is called.
Cycle attach attempts are rejected with typed LineageCycle and ledgered as an anomaly.
Parent termination with cascade_cancel cancels all live descendants depth-first via coordinator cancellation, each with a ledger row; orphan mode leaves children live and marks rows orphaned.
children_of / parent_of / ancestor_chain / live_tree queries return correct results for a 3-level fixture tree.
Attach/detach enrich existing FR-EVT-SWARM-* event payloads with lineage fields; no new event kinds are minted in this MT.
proof_targets: cargo sqlx migrate run && cargo sqlx migrate revert (or the project's migration runner equivalent) green against managed PostgreSQL
expected_tests: unit: depth calculation over a synthetic chain; cycle detection over a forged ancestor set
integration (managed PG): attach on spawn, row rolled back when spawn_session rejects
integration (managed PG): cascade_cancel on parent termination cancels grandchildren before children, all ledgered
integration (managed PG): orphan policy leaves child live with orphaned row state
negative: direct lineage write from a tool surface is impossible (no such API exported)
implementation_notes: Migration numbering: inspect the migrations directory at implementation time and take the next free numeric prefix; do not renumber existing migrations. The directory currently extends well past 0070 (verified 2026-07-21); the exact next number is decided at merge time.
spawned_by_actor also records operator- and scheduler-initiated spawns so the MT-107 tree can show the whole forest, but only model-initiated rows participate in MT-106 policy accounting.
Depth default 2 keeps workers leaf-only; raising it is an operator config decision surfaced through MT-106's override surface.
Cascade must tolerate already-terminated children (idempotent cancel), and a cascade failure on one child must not silently skip the rest (HBR-SWARM-002 no-silent-loss: record per-child outcome).
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-001 session model, MT-161 FR kinds (any new lineage-specific event ids), MT-106 policy (orphan opt-in gating), MT-107 GUI consumer.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless persistence + lifecycle MT; the operator-visible tree ships in MT-107.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal registry with no direct operator-facing behavior change; MT-107 documents the visible session tree and cascade semantics in the same change as its GUI.

risk_if_missed: No durable lineage: steer scoping (MT-102) has no canonical authority, terminated parents leak running children (silent loss + cost burn), recursive self-spawn depth is unbounded below the global caps, and the session-tree GUI has nothing truthful to render.

risks: RISK-1: Orphan leak — parent dies, cascade fails midway or is skipped, children keep running unattributed and burning budget with nobody steering them.
RISK-2: Depth-limit bypass — depth computed from a stale or partial chain (e.g. missing intermediate row) lets a model spawn deeper than configured.
RISK-3: Lineage forgery — a code path other than the spawn handler writes lineage rows, poisoning steer-scope checks and the GUI tree.
RISK-4: Cascade as a weapon — a parent deliberately terminates to cascade-cancel children mid-write, corrupting worker output without trace.
RISK-5: Registry/coordinator drift — registry says live, coordinator says terminated (or vice versa), and consumers act on the wrong view.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Cascade executor records a per-child outcome row; any per-child failure is a typed, ledgered anomaly and the remaining children are still processed; test kills a mid-tree parent and asserts full descendant accounting.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Depth computed transactionally from the ancestor chain at attach time; missing-ancestor is a typed integrity error, not depth 0; unit test with a gapped chain.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): attach/detach are crate-private and called only from the spawn/terminate paths; no public or tool-exposed write API (asserted by a negative test and API review).

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Cascade cancellation is the coordinator's cooperative cancel (workers get their normal cancellation semantics, ledgered with reason=parent_cascade); MT-108 asserts the FR trail makes the cause attributable.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): terminated_at is written from coordinator terminal events (single source); live_tree cross-checks coordinator state and flags divergence as a typed diagnostic.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: migrations/ directory layout (numeric-prefix pairs, e.g. 0019_kernel_session_queue, 0021_kernel_process_lifecycle), ids.rs SpawnRequest.parent_session_id (existing lineage attribution field), coordinator.rs (terminal states, CancellationToken, teardown ownership), events.rs (SESSION-CANCELLED/COMPLETED/FAILED events to enrich). External precedent: process-group/cgroup cascade semantics and Claude Code subagent lifecycle (children bounded by parent lifetime by default).
